source.version: Journal version of record: Electronics 2025, 14(15), 2955, published 24 July 2025 (received 27 June 2025, revised 21 July 2025, accepted 22 July 2025)
source.title_on_document: Story Forge: A Card-Based Framework for AI-Assisted Interactive Storytelling

supplement.where: No supplementary material is referenced. Appendix A (pp. 31-32) is in this PDF and holds example story excerpts only. Data Availability Statement (p. 31): data at University of Plymouth's OneDrive, no URL given.

paper_design_summary: Thirty university students were randomly divided into a control condition that used a web-based AI story generator (Squibler AI Story Writer) and an experimental condition that used Story Forge, the authors' card-based interface built on the Doubao 3.5 LLM API; sessions ran in groups of five and lasted 35 minutes. Outcomes are interaction-log metrics (dwell time, decisions, path complexity, choice coverage, causal relationship strength, revisits, new path discovery) and self-reported questionnaires (SUS, Creativity Support Index, User Participation Index). No rater or computed score of the creativity or diversity of the stories is reported.

studies.label: Comparative experiment: Story Forge vs AI Story Writer (interactive story writing)

assignment.what_was_assigned: Which AI story-writing tool the participant used: Story Forge (card-based interface on Doubao 3.5) or the web-based AI Story Writer (Squibler)
assignment.quote: Participants were randomly divided into a control group and an experimental group.
assignment.locator: p. 19, Section 4.3 (Demographic Data); also Abstract, p. 1

arms.name: Experimental group (Story Forge)
arms.description: Card-based adaptive story interface (Unity front end, Doubao 3.5 LLM back end); participants drag character, event, emotion and scene cards into slots and the AI generates branching story text.

arms.name: Control group (AI Story Writer)
arms.description: Web-based AI story generator (AI Story Writer, Squibler 2025) with a predetermined story theme and creation duration.

participants.exclusions: None reported. Result tables (Tables 6-9) print no n. The paper states 30 story drafts at the end, 15 per condition (p. 21), and describes 'a sample of 30 participants' (p. 29). Per-arm 15 follows from three groups of five per condition (p. 19-20). n_analyzed = 30 rests on these statements, not on an analysis count printed with the results.
participants.who: University students (15 male, 15 female) with expertise in AI tools and story creation (M = 2.53, SD = 0.95); none had used the systems before. Section 5.6 (p. 29) instead describes the sample as '70% students' with writing experience mean = 15.4 years, which conflicts with p. 19.
participants.country: not_stated (authors at University of Plymouth, UK)
participants.quote: We enrolled 30 university students (15 males, 15 females) with expertise in AI tools and story creation (M = 2.53, SD = 0.95) into a study.
participants.locator: p. 19, Section 4.3; p. 20 (power analysis, 30 recruited); p. 21, Section 4.5 (30 story drafts, 15 per group)

ai_tool.name_model: Story Forge on Doubao AI LLM (version 3.5, ByteDance) vs AI Story Writer (Squibler 2025, model not stated)
ai_tool.how_used: Both arms used generative AI to write stories. In Story Forge the participant combines story-element cards and the LLM generates branching plot text from a structured prompt built from the cards; in AI Story Writer the participant enters a plot prompt and genre and the tool generates the story.

task.description: Interactive story creation: story creation, plot expansion, and branching plot development on a predetermined theme.
task.duration: 35 min session after a 10 min training session; interviews averaged 25 min

outcomes.name: Exploration path complexity (number of branches)
outcomes.question: none
outcomes.measure_detail: Number of branch nodes / path length from 'Quantitative Analysis of Path Structure' of interaction logs; the paper classifies it under User Engagement (Table 4, p. 19). Not a creativity score.

contrasts.reported: Control 7.2 ± 2.7 vs Experimental 11.0 ± 3.5; t = 5.12, p = 0.022, 'Significant'. No d printed in text; Figure 13 forest plot shows no row for it. Per-arm n not printed in the table.

outcomes.name: Choice coverage rate (pathway %)
outcomes.question: none
outcomes.measure_detail: Proportion of triggered paths from content mining of logs (Table 4, p. 19). The paper names it one of 'two primary metrics' for the FDR correction (p. 25).

contrasts.reported: Control 52.9 ± 13.9 vs Experimental 70.4 ± 15.0; t = 5.58, p = 0.012; d = 1.21; BH-FDR adjusted p = 0.024. 95% CI shown only in Figure 13.
contrasts.locator: p. 22, Table 7; p. 24-25, Section 5.2; p. 26, Figure 13

outcomes.name: Causal relationship strength (0-1)
outcomes.question: none
outcomes.measure_detail: 'Causal Relationship Reasonableness Diagram (Node Connection Strength)' from 'Quantitative Analysis of Logical Relationship Diagram' (Table 4, p. 19). The text interprets it as users' comprehension / 'perceived causal relationship strength' (pp. 22, 25), so whether it scores the story itself is unclear. Not a creativity measure.

contrasts.reported: Control 0.74 ± 0.15 vs Experimental 0.76 ± 0.14; t = 0.63, p = 0.531, 'Not significant'; d = 0.14; FDR-adjusted p = 0.531.
contrasts.locator: p. 22, Table 7; p. 24-25, Section 5.2; p. 26, Figure 13

outcomes.name: New path discovery rate (%)
outcomes.question: none
outcomes.measure_detail: Proportion of new paths from unlocked path statistics (Table 4, p. 19); classified under Replay Value.

contrasts.locator: p. 23, Table 8; p. 25, Section 5.2; p. 26, Figure 13

outcomes.name: Creativity Support Index (CSI), self-reported
outcomes.question: none
outcomes.measure_detail: Post-task questionnaire; described as 36 items across 6 dimensions on a 7-point scale (p. 18), but Table 4 lists a 1-5 point rating system and reported means are on roughly a 1-5 range. Self-report of the tool's creativity support, not a score of the stories. Listed only to document why criterion 3 fails.

contrasts.reported: Control 3.5 ± 0.8 vs Experimental 3.9 ± 0.7; t = 2.48, p = 0.041; d = 0.53; BH-FDR corrected p = 0.061 (not significant after correction).
contrasts.locator: p. 24, Table 9; p. 25, Section 5.2; p. 26, Figure 13

data_and_code.data_url: Not given as a URL: 'The data can be found at University of Plymouth's OneDrive.' (p. 31)

eligibility.reason: Individuals were randomly divided between two generative-AI story tools (an ai_design contrast), so criterion 1 is met. Only 30 students took part (p. 19), well below 50. No outcome scores the creativity or diversity of the stories: outcomes are interaction-log engagement metrics and self-report scales, and the authors state the evaluation lacks 'third-party objective assessment of the quality of the content that is produced' (p. 29).

one_line_finding: In a 30-student randomized comparison of two AI story tools, Story Forge users had higher choice coverage (70.4 vs 52.9 percent, d = 1.21, p = 0.012) and higher self-reported Creativity Support Index (3.9 vs 3.5, d = 0.53, FDR p = 0.061), with no creativity score of the stories (pp. 22-25, Tables 7 and 9).
open_questions: The reported t and p values are internally inconsistent with n = 15 per arm (e.g., t = 5.41 with p = 0.015, t = 5.58 with p = 0.012, Table 6-7, p. 22); the statistics may be unreliable.
Sample description conflicts: p. 19 says 30 university students; p. 29 says '70% students' with writing experience mean = 15.4 years.
CSI scale described as 7-point with 36 items (p. 18) but Table 4 (p. 19) lists 1-5 point scoring.
Sessions were run in groups of five (three groups per condition, p. 20); analysis treats participants as independent with no adjustment for session.

p. 21 says collaboration levels were rated by two trained raters, but no rater results are reported; p. 21 also lists possible output metrics (word count, diversity of story elements) that are not reported.
notes: Outcomes left out of the outcomes list because they are clearly not creativity measures: story writing dwell time, number of decisions (Table 6), repeat visit rate (Table 8), SUS and UPI (Table 9). Section 3.6 (pp. 15-17) qualitatively compares Story Forge with GPT-4o and NovelAI using one example narrative, with no participants and no scored outcome. Section 5.6 (p. 29) says homogenization (Doshi and Hauser 2024) 'was not thoroughly explored in this study'.
